200	Extremely serious, and people, a baal teshuvah, who calls himself a rabbi, oh
201	woe to us, "our dispute is Your dispute, and our judgment is Your judgment."
202	Therefore, a person who has holiness and closeness to HaShem must guard it
203	more than anything!
204	You have a soul-friend, a merciful Father who loves you.
205	You have a relationship with Him of love, of devotion, of closeness, of speech.
206	Is that the most important thing to you in the world?
207	Don't sell it for a pot of lentil stew.
208	Don't sell it for a pot of lentil stew.
209	And every millimeter forward that you can get closer in a relationship with Him, even if it costs you blood,
210	tears, fasts, "your heart and your blood you shall pour out" — pour it out and draw close to Him.
211	The main thing is to be more His friend, closer to Him.
212	Don't they tell of Rabbi Eliyahu Mani, peace be upon him? They called him a chasid, and why was he a chasid? Because every
213	pious practice he could take, he took upon himself. Once Rabbi Efraim Cohen told, and why would he take on pious practices?
214	In order to cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He, to come a little closer to Him, one more millimeter. Once he was studying
215	Etz Chaim and didn't understand, reviewed it and still didn't understand. He opened the window, not knowing
216	that the room wasn't empty. His yeshivah was in Hebron.
217	He was the rabbi of Hebron, and one of the rabbis was there, the door was
218	open, and he saw the rabbi open the window and say: Master of the worlds, I don't understand. How many
219	fasts have I already fasted, how many mortifications have I already undertaken. What more do You want me to take upon myself
220	that I haven't taken? Look at what this is, where he got to: what more do You
221	want me to take upon myself that I haven't taken?
222	I have already taken on every pious practice I can; I stretched myself to the limit of my ability.
223	That is how a person who serves HaShem, who draws close to the Holy One, blessed be He, as much as he can, is stringent upon himself.
224	Not everything lenient, everything "they were accustomed to be lenient"; those are laws for after the fact.
225	There are some who are experts in the laws of after the fact.
226	After the fact it's possible, but after the fact it's permitted.
227	Haven't I told you a thousand times that someone will call me?
228	He asks me some question, permitted or forbidden. I told him forbidden. He says to me, Rabbi,
229	think again. Tell me, are you serious? I tell you,
230	forbidden. He says to me, maybe still you'll find some way to permit it. I told him,
231	this is the Gemara, the Yerushalmi, Shulchan Aruch and Rambam — all ruled it is forbidden. He says to me, ya Allah, you
232	are already the eighth rabbi to tell me that it is forbidden. Have mercy, what are you looking for?
233	A scapegoat in your place to go to Azazel?
234	To go to Gehenom in your place?
235	What are you? Forbidden is forbidden. There are those who are experts in the laws of after the fact.
236	Listen, but after the fact it's permitted, but after the fact there is one who was accustomed to be lenient, but after the fact, but after the fact.
237	Instead of being one who distances himself from a hundred gates of after-the-fact, for the sake of a hundred
238	gates of permissibility, so as not to stumble in a single after-the-fact case.
